correctness.rationale: The all-angle proof starts from (I-R)z∈Z² and the exact half-angle inverse. For positive sine, the integer labels are bounded by a∈{1,2}, b∈{0,1} except the origin, and every candidate is individually checked against [0,1)^2; half-turn and opposite orientation are treated separately. The invariant open disks remain in one reduction branch and rotate exactly, radii equal distance to boundary, and explicit separations prove their disjointness. Twenty-three rational-angle exact checks include thresholds but do not substitute for the analytic argument.

value.rationale: The nearest same mathematical model literature proves existence of nontrivial fixed points on a sufficient angular range but does not quantify the full angle dependence. The result provides a complete natural fixed-point bifurcation classification, three strict birth thresholds, exact geometric locations and an invariant-area law for canonical disjoint islands. Those disks support explicit mutually singular absolutely continuous invariant probabilities and quantify the regular portion of a discontinuous torus-reduced rotation across all angles; no arbitrary parameter slice or known-table recomputation is used.
